comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Recovery record (2026-09-02, by the agent session that hit this outage).

I was blocked pushing a Gerrit stack for ~5h and diagnosed the host from the AWS API only, since there was no shell: the SSM agent showed `ConnectionLost` with last ping **03:09:52 PDT**.

What ruled things IN and OUT:

* EC2 status checks `ok` for both instance and system throughout -> hypervisor and instance networking healthy, so the `rebar-gerrit-ec2-*-check` alarms structurally cannot catch this class.
* `unlimited` burstable, `CPUCreditBalance` ~440 and `CPUSurplusCreditBalance` 0.0 -> CPU throttling ruled out.
* CPU held a normal 20-50% the whole time -> the kernel never wedged; `get-console-output --latest` confirmed a live console (uptime ~11.9h) with continuous Docker veth churn, no OOM kills and no I/O errors.
* TCP 443 stayed OPEN while HTTP went 504 -> then -> SSL timeout. The reverse proxy outlived its upstream, which is why black-box probes saw slow failure rather than connection refusal, and why `git push` reported 504 before it reported nothing.
* `rebar/host` `root_disk_used_percent` climbing 87 -> 94% and then STOPPING mid-series, with `GerritReachable` stopping at the same timestamp -> root disk full, publisher dead.

Recovery, chosen because it needs no shell:

1. `create-snapshot` -> `snap-06f35ff3a20fe4a73` (root `vol-0270fcf13709cf472`), for reversibility.
2. `modify-volume` 30 -> 60 GiB; reached `optimizing` in ~16s, which is already usable.
3. `reboot-instances`. AL2023 cloud-init runs `growpart` at boot, so the partition AND filesystem expanded with no shell.
4. Back at **07:10 PDT**: HTTP 200, SSM `Online`, `/dev/nvme0n1p1 60G 29G 32G 48% /`.

The Elastic IP (`eipalloc-0bfd9c30897fc366a`) meant a stop/start would also have been address-safe, but reboot was sufficient and less disruptive.

**This is an unwedge and must not be recorded as the fix.** The 29 GiB working set is untouched; only headroom changed, 97%+ -> 48%. Whatever produced 29 GiB on a 30 GiB disk will produce 60 GiB on a 60 GiB disk.

AC3 is still open because I could not capture the breakdown: every `du -xh /` and `docker system df` invocation I sent hung in `InProgress` on the freshly rebooted, IO-loaded box, while trivial commands (`df`, `lsblk`) returned immediately. That measurement should be taken while the host is idle. `lsblk` did confirm the 50-GiB data volume `nvme1n1` carries the `gerrit_git`, `gerrit_index`, `gerrit_logs`, `gerrit_plugins` and `gerrit_etc` Docker volumes, so the 29 GiB on ROOT is not Gerrit's repo data — it is Docker images/layers/build cache, which is consistent with every prior incident in the chain.

One consequence worth noting for the gate-economics record: the outage cost a real false signal. Yesterday's `preodorous-temporary-piglet` records change 2481 burning its retry budget into a **spurious `LLM-Review -1`** from ENOSPC. Disk pressure on this host does not merely slow reviews, it manufactures incorrect review verdicts.

comments.body:
AC3 measurement, captured once the host was idle enough to answer `du` (07:5x PDT, after the unwedge, so these are the SAME bytes that filled the 30-GiB disk — only the denominator changed).

```
/            28G
  /var       26G
    /var/lib          21G
      /var/lib/docker 17G
        overlay2      16G      <-- 67 layer directories
        volumes      929M
        buildkit      86M
        image        7.7M
    /var/tmp         3.6G
    /var/log         1.8G      (journal 1.7G)
    /var/cache       154M
  /usr        1.9G
```

Docker's OWN accounting for the same tree:

```
TYPE            TOTAL  ACTIVE  SIZE      RECLAIMABLE
Images          4      4       2.802GB   144.4MB (5%)
Containers      4      4       4.815GB   0B (0%)
Local Volumes   11     1       962.2MB   1.207MB (0%)
Build Cache     41     0       920.4MB   920.4MB
```
`docker images -f dangling=true -q | wc -l` -> **0**

## This is why four rounds of prune-based mitigation did not hold

Docker accounts for ~9.5 GB. `overlay2` on disk is **16 GB**. About **6.5 GB is orphaned layer state that Docker does not know it owns** — 67 layer directories backing only 4 images and 4 containers, with ZERO dangling images.

`docker system prune` frees only what the table calls RECLAIMABLE: **144 MB + 920 MB ~= 1.06 GB**, about 3.5% of the 29 GB working set. The pressure-triggered prune added in `sour-plugugly-rhino` and hardened in later tickets was therefore structurally incapable of recovering the disk, no matter how often or how early it fired. Every incident in this chain re-tuned the TRIGGER for a reclaim whose CEILING was ~1 GB against a 29 GB problem.

And the root disk has **three independent accumulators**, only one of which prune touches at all:

1. **orphaned `overlay2` layers** — ~6.5 GB invisible to prune (needs the daemon's own GC, or a stop-daemon + orphan sweep).
2. **`/var/tmp` — 3.6 GB** — not Docker's at all; never touched by any prune. Consistent with `scowlful-bovine-dragonfly`'s finding that one-off investigation evidence lands on disk and is never swept.
3. **journald — 1.7 GB** — no `SystemMaxUse` cap in effect; also never touched by prune.

So AC4's "bounded ceiling, not faster reclaim" should be read strictly: a fix that only makes prune more eager repeats this bug a fifth time. The ceiling has to bind all three accumulators — a journald `SystemMaxUse=`, a `/var/tmp` retention sweep, and an overlay2 reclaim that can actually reach orphaned layers.

Note also that the ~9.5 GB Docker DOES account for is dominated by **4.815 GB of container writable layers with 0 B reclaimable** — long-lived containers accumulating writes inside their own layers. Restarting/recreating containers is what releases that, which is likely why a reboot has historically appeared to "fix" this for a while and then not.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Phase 1 RCA for scoped Defect 2 only (paging gap). Step 0(a): searched `cyclopean`, `root disk outage missing data`, and open/in_progress bugs; this ticket is the live report and prior hits are related disk-pressure incidents, not a duplicate Defect-2 paging-gap ticket. Step 0(b): no version in report; created_at 1788360014874178001 maps to floor commit 8f19115cf2fb0c7e3411a1b8d932899bc9b1dc27. Suspect alarm files changed before that floor, not after. Step 0(c): debug worktree HEAD 952f0825321c755f41edce412ad1fe9f1db9268d equals origin/main.

Confirmed root cause: the two host-published disk alarms are Terraform-managed and encode the dead-man switch backward. `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf` defines `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.root_disk_pressure` / `rebar-root-disk-pressure` on `rebar/host:root_disk_used_percent` with `alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]` but `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"`; `infra/terraform/monitoring.tf` defines `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.gerrit_data_disk_high` / `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` the same way for `rebar/host:disk_used_percent` mount=/var/gerrit. Live AWS matches the code: `describe-alarms` returned TreatMissingData=notBreaching for both, with AlarmActions/OKActions wired to `arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:896586841071:rebar-gerrit-alerts`; that topic has a confirmed email subscription to joeoakhart@navapbc.com. The alarm-notification path is therefore present; the missing-data classification is the broken artifact.

Discriminating evidence: CloudWatch metric data has no `root_disk_used_percent` or `GerritReachable` datapoints between 2026-09-02 01:40 PDT and 07:10 PDT. `rebar-root-disk-pressure` history shows ALARM -> OK at 01:45 PDT, then no further state update during the outage. `rebar-gerrit-gate-down`, whose TreatMissingData is breaching, moved OK -> ALARM at 02:05 with reason "no datapoints were received for 2 periods and 2 missing datapoints were treated as [Breaching]". That rules out missing SNS wiring as the Defect-2 cause and isolates the disk alarms' `notBreaching` setting.

Defect legitimacy: defect. The ticket's AC1 explicitly requires the disk alarms to stop treating missing data as healthy, and `monitoring.tf` already documents the intended dead-probe behavior for host-published health metrics on `gerrit_gate_down`: missing data is breaching because absence means the host/probe is not known healthy.

Origin attribution for Defect 2: root alarm line introduced by commit 7ed670b0342db0132ea7d41fe8a013cdc386cedf (`rebar-ticket: ac14-363f-4ba0-4b5c`) with the incorrect "don't double-page on host loss" assumption; data-disk alarm line introduced by commit 5e1a59491f2ea5c7de55c6d7db972d8207acddcc (`rebar-ticket: c7d4`) copying the same assumption. Because this ticket will not be closed in this scoped pass, I am recording both origins here rather than closing with a single `--caused-by`.

Phase 2 plan for scoped Defect 2: change both disk alarms' `treat_missing_data` to `breaching`, update the adjacent comments to state that stopped host-published disk metrics page through the existing SNS alarm_actions, and extend the existing Terraform alarm guard test to prevent reintroducing notBreaching on these alarms. No live AWS mutation will be performed by this agent; Terraform apply / induced publish-stop verification remains an operator/live-deploy step after Gerrit merge.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

On 2026-09-02 the `rebar-gerrit` host (`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`, us-east-1) filled its 30-GiB gp3 root volume and took **Gerrit fully offline for ~5 hours** (~02:05–07:10 PDT). This is the FOURTH root-disk-pressure incident in a month and the FIRST to cause a complete outage: previous incidents degraded the review bot, this one killed the service, the SSM agent, and the metrics publisher simultaneously.

Two distinct defects. The second is new and is the reason nobody was paged.

## Defect 1 — root disk fills faster than reclaim frees it

Root reached **29 GiB used of 30 GiB**. Every prior mitigation has reduced the rate without bounding the ceiling, so the disk still reaches 100%.

## Defect 2 (NEW, and the reason this became a 5-hour outage) — the disk alarm RESET ITSELF TO OK as the host died

`rebar-root-disk-pressure` is configured:

* metric `rebar/host` `root_disk_used_percent`, threshold **> 85%**
* **EvaluationPeriods = 3**
* **TreatMissingData = `notBreaching`**

The metric is published BY AN AGENT ON THE HOST THAT IS RUNNING OUT OF DISK. Observed series (30-min max):

```
2026-09-01T23:03  92
2026-09-01T23:33  94      <- breaching (>85)
2026-09-02T00:03  92
2026-09-02T00:33  91
2026-09-02T01:03  92
2026-09-02T01:33  90      <- LAST DATAPOINT EVER
(no data thereafter)
```

`GerritReachable` stops at the same timestamp. The publisher died with the host.

Because the disk was breaching but had not yet accumulated **3** breaching periods, and because missing data is treated as **notBreaching**, the alarm did not fire — it transitioned **to `OK` at 01:45:10**, i.e. it went GREEN at the exact moment the host became unreachable, and is STILL green now. The only thing that fired was `rebar-gerrit-gate-down` (a black-box reachability probe) at 02:05.

This is the classic dead-man's-switch inversion: for a metric published by the failing host, "no data" is the strongest possible evidence of the condition, and this configuration reads it as the absence of the condition. `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` has the SAME `notBreaching` setting and the same inversion.

## Why the prior fixes did not hold

Chronology (all on this host, all root disk unless noted):

* **2026-08-04/06** — `sour-plugugly-rhino` (28f9-535c-ce9c-4583): root 48% -> 95%, pinned 92–96% for ~39h. Fix: pressure-triggered `docker prune` on the autodeploy no-op tick.
* **2026-08-17** — `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` (3a52-2d79-320d-4fed): root 71% -> 90%, review-bot unhealthy. Title records this as happening **"after automated-reclaim mitigation"** — the Aug-4 prune did not prevent it.
* **2026-08-26** — `/var/gerrit` DATA volume fill; remediation task `scowlful-bovine-dragonfly` (3e92-b7f4-dede-4c17) is **still OPEN**.
* **2026-08-29/30** — `beton-naval-eyas` (2f46-6871-796f-41c9): correlated autodeploy alarms on this host.
* **2026-09-01 (yesterday)** — `preodorous-temporary-piglet` (3cef-c948-68ba-40fd): root 91–95%, review clones hit ENOSPC, change 2481 burned its retry budget into a **spurious `LLM-Review -1`**.
* **2026-09-02 (today)** — full outage, ~5h.

Reclaim has been made *faster* and *more triggered* each round, but nothing has ever bounded the CEILING, and no alarm survives the host it monitors.

## Recovery performed (an UNWEDGE, not a fix)

1. Snapshot `snap-06f35ff3a20fe4a73` of root `vol-0270fcf13709cf472`.
2. `modify-volume` root **30 -> 60 GiB**.
3. Reboot; AL2023 cloud-init `growpart` expanded partition + filesystem at boot.
4. Verified: `/dev/nvme0n1p1 60G 29G 32G 48% /`; Gerrit HTTP 200 and SSM `Online` at 07:10 PDT.

**The 29 GiB of content is UNCHANGED — this only bought headroom.** At the observed fill rate the larger disk postpones recurrence, it does not prevent it. Growing the volume must not be recorded as the resolution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 [non-codebase]: `rebar-root-disk-pressure` and `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` no longer treat missing data as healthy — `TreatMissingData` becomes `breaching` (or `missing`), so a host that stops publishing raises rather than clears. Verified by `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` showing the new setting, and by an induced publish-stop raising the alarm.
- [ ] AC2 [non-codebase]: the disk alarm fires BEFORE the host is unrecoverable — an alarm exists that would have fired on the 2026-09-01T23:33 94% datapoint. Verified by replaying the recorded series against the new threshold/period configuration.
- [ ] AC3: the top consumer of the 29 GiB root working set is identified and named with measured byte totals (the `du`/`docker system df` breakdown could not be captured during recovery because SSM invocations hung on the loaded box).
- [ ] AC4: root usage has a bounded CEILING, not merely a faster reclaim — a mechanism that cannot exceed a configured high-water mark regardless of build burst rate. Verified by a test or simulation driving the documented fill rate and showing usage plateaus below the bound.
- [ ] AC5: the still-open `/var/gerrit` remediation `scowlful-bovine-dragonfly` is either completed or explicitly superseded by this ticket's fix, so the data volume is not left with the same unbounded shape.
- [ ] AC6 [non-codebase]: an operator runbook entry covers "host is wedged and SSM is ConnectionLost", recording the shell-free recovery path used here (snapshot -> modify-volume -> reboot -> cloud-init growpart) and stating explicitly that it is an unwedge requiring a follow-up reclaim.

## Notes

- The EC2 status checks stayed `ok` throughout: the hypervisor and instance networking were healthy, so instance-check alarms cannot detect this class.
- The instance is `unlimited` burstable with ~440 CPU credits and 0 surplus, so CPU throttling was ruled out as a cause.
- TCP 443 stayed OPEN while HTTP returned 504 then timed out — the reverse proxy survived while its upstream died, which is why black-box probes saw a slow failure rather than a refusal.
